title: Unauthenticated pickle deserialization from the basket cookie
description: The basket cookie is client-controlled and unsigned, but is decoded with pickle.loads(). A crafted cookie can execute attacker-controlled Python code whenever a basket endpoint reads it.
evidence: read_basket() base64-decodes request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads() at shopapi/basket.py:15-23. with_basket() writes an ordinary base64-encoded pickle at lines 26-28 without authentication or signing. The public GET /basket endpoint invokes read_basket().

title: Authentication failures are swallowed, allowing protected handlers to continue
description: require_auth catches the 401 exception raised when authentication fails and then invokes the protected handler with g.user set to None. Protected handlers that do not immediately dereference g.user are therefore reachable without authentication.
evidence: The broad except at shopapi/auth.py:55-58 catches abort(401) from line 54 and returns f() anyway. A request without Authorization to GET /orders/3 returned HTTP 200 with order details, while the same flaw exposes GET /giftcards/HFDEMO10.

title: Order detail endpoint does not enforce ownership
description: The order detail handler uses get_order() rather than own_order(), so an authenticated customer can retrieve another customer's order details. Combined with the fail-open authentication decorator, unauthenticated callers can also retrieve them.
evidence: show_order() at shopapi/orders.py:46-49 returns order_json(get_order(order_id)); the ownership check exists only in own_order() at lines 32-36 and is not called. GET /orders/3 without credentials returned the order's items, totals, delivery date and refunds.

title: Trailing-slash admin refund route bypasses staff authorization
description: The global admin check compares the literal request path to registered route rules. The refund route accepts a trailing slash due to strict_slashes=False, but the trailing-slash path is not in the exact rule set, allowing the handler to run without the staff check.
evidence: shopapi/__init__.py:26-41 builds admin_paths from route rules and checks request.path for exact membership. shopapi/admin.py:51-53 registers /admin/refunds with strict_slashes=False, while goodwill_refund() performs a refund at lines 55-67 without its own authorization check.

title: Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection
description: The q parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL statement instead of being bound as a parameter, allowing an attacker to alter the WHERE clause and retrieve unintended records.
evidence: shopapi/products.py:40-42 constructs SQL by concatenating q into LIKE expressions. GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1%20-- returned all six products instead of only matching products.

title: Stored display names enable second-order SQL injection in the staff report
description: A customer's stored display_name is interpolated into a SQL query when staff request the review report. A customer can save SQL syntax as their display name and have it interpreted later in the administrative query.
evidence: display_name is accepted and stored by update_account() at shopapi/auth.py:119-125. reviews_by_customer() inserts customer['display_name'] into an f-string SQL WHERE clause at shopapi/admin.py:77-80 instead of binding it.

title: Stored XSS in review bodies
description: Review bodies are stored without sanitization and rendered as trusted HTML, allowing an authenticated user to inject script or event-handler markup that executes for visitors viewing the product page.
evidence: add_review() inserts the submitted body directly at shopapi/products.py:90-91. shopapi/templates/product.html renders the review body with the Jinja safe filter, so the stored value is not escaped.

title: Image import follows redirects to unvalidated destinations
description: The image importer validates only the initial URL's hostname and public DNS result. requests.get() follows redirects by default, so an approved host that redirects can make the server fetch an internal or metadata address.
evidence: check_url() validates only the original parsed URL at shopapi/images.py:28-35, then import_image() calls requests.get(url, timeout=10, stream=True) at line 50 without allow_redirects=False or revalidating redirect targets.

title: Checkout does not enforce or decrement stock
description: Checkout creates order items from the client-controlled basket and current prices without checking product stock or updating it. Repeated customers can therefore place orders for unavailable quantities and oversell inventory indefinitely.
evidence: basket_json() reads product rows and calculates totals at shopapi/basket.py:32-41 but never checks stock. checkout() inserts order items at lines 69-73 and no stock update occurs anywhere in that flow.

title: Returns ignore previously cancelled quantities
description: The return validation compares returned quantity only with the original quantity and ignores cancelled_qty. Units already cancelled and refunded can therefore be returned and refunded a second time after delivery.
evidence: cancel_items() increments cancelled_qty at shopapi/orders.py:65-68. return_items() accepts a return when returned_qty + qty <= item.qty at lines 90-93 and refunds qty * price at lines 94-96, without subtracting cancelled_qty.

title: Payment timeout fails open and marks orders as paid
description: A timeout from the payment provider is explicitly converted to status='paid', after which the order is moved to processing and credited for its full total. Provider outages or induced timeouts can create unpaid fulfillable orders.
evidence: confirm_payment() catches requests.Timeout and sets status = 'paid' at shopapi/payments.py:39-42. Lines 43-46 then set the order to processing and paid_pence=total_pence.

title: Payment webhook authenticates only the order ID and trusts the amount
description: The webhook signature covers only order_id. Once a signature is accepted, the request can supply any status amount and the handler stores amount_pence without comparing it to the order total or a provider-verified transaction.
evidence: webhook_signature() signs only str(order_id) at shopapi/payments.py:53-55; payment_webhook() verifies that value at line 63 and assigns int(event.get('amount_pence', 0)) directly to paid_pence at lines 69-71.

title: Token refresh accepts unsigned and expired JWTs
description: The refresh endpoint disables signature verification and does not require a valid expiration claim. Anyone can fabricate an unsigned token containing an existing user ID and obtain a newly signed token with that user's role.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:101 calls jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False}); the untrusted sub is used to load a user at line 104 and make_token() issues a fresh token at line 107.

title: Hardcoded JWT signing secret
description: The JWT signing key is fixed in source code. Anyone who obtains the source or package can forge tokens, including tokens claiming the staff role.
evidence: config.py:3 sets SECRET_KEY = 'hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d'; shopapi/auth.py uses it for both token signing at line 27 and verification at line 42.

title: Predictable default webhook secret permits forged payment events
description: When WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured, the application uses the publicly guessable value whsec-local. An attacker can calculate valid webhook signatures and forge payment events.
evidence: config.py:8 uses os.environ.get('WEBHOOK_SECRET', 'whsec-local'). The webhook derives its only signature from this secret and the attacker-supplied order ID at shopapi/payments.py:53-55.

title: Passwords are stored using unsalted SHA-256
description: Passwords are hashed with a fast unsalted digest and no work factor. A database compromise therefore enables rapid offline cracking of common or reused passwords.
evidence: hash_password() returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() at shopapi/auth.py:15-16, and check_password() compares raw digests at lines 19-20.

title: Password reset codes lack brute-force protection
description: Reset codes are eight decimal digits generated with the non-cryptographic random module, remain valid for 30 minutes, and have no attempt counter or rate limiting. Repeated guesses can eventually reset an account password.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:135 generates the code with random.random() and an eight-digit format; reset_confirm() checks guesses at lines 143-161 without counting failures or applying rate limits.

title: Concurrent gift-card redemptions can overspend a card
description: Redemption reads the balance, checks the requested amount, computes a new balance, and later writes it without a row lock or conditional balance update. Concurrent requests can both pass the check and record redemptions against the same balance.
evidence: shopapi/giftcards.py:36-43 performs the balance check, calculates new_balance, inserts the redemption, and unconditionally updates the card. The SQLite connection has no transaction-level conditional update protecting this sequence.

title: Request logging records passwords and other sensitive request data
description: The request hook logs complete POST, PUT, and PATCH bodies, including plaintext login and registration passwords, reset codes and new passwords, and potentially payment data. Anyone with log access can recover these secrets.
evidence: shopapi/__init__.py:28-31 calls request.get_data(as_text=True)[:2000] for every write request with no endpoint-specific redaction.
